clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old male with diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease presented to the Emergency Department with four months of unintentional 25-pound weight loss and four days of persistent hiccups, denying fever or respiratory symptoms. Chest X-ray on admission demonstrated new bilateral ground-glass opacities involving the right upper lung, left mid and lower lungs, and right costophrenic angle (E001). Laboratory evaluation revealed leukopenia (4,200 cells), thrombocytopenia (15,000 platelets), hyponatremia (131 mEq/L), and hypochloremia (98 mEq/L) (E003). He was admitted to the COVID medical unit as a person under investigation, placed in isolation, and empirically treated with ceftriaxone and azithromycin (E004). Upon arrival to the medical unit, he was febrile to 38.4°C and tachycardic to 104 bpm, and was started on hydroxychloroquine 400 mg BID for one day followed by 200 mg BID for five days for suspected COVID-19 infection (E005). He received symptomatic care and was discharged three days after admission in stable condition (E007).
